skill: mrwadams/threat-led-triage skills/threat-led-triage (pinned); references/scoring.md applied by hand
run: 2026-10-11 over every VULN and VERIFY record in review/findings/*.json, with review/stride/agent.json as the threat model (the STRIDE GPT model is owed: no model key in this session) and the register's actors as the trust boundaries

reachability_vocabulary.host: A1 alone: the SG/Send host, a mirror, or whoever compromised either; no key needed (the equivalent of `unauthenticated` for this system: the one party the design says to distrust)
reachability_vocabulary.read-key: A3 + A1: a read-key holder who can also write to the store
reachability_vocabulary.writer: A4: a teammate with the write key (authenticated)
reachability_vocabulary.author: A5: a hostile vault author
reachability_vocabulary.local: A6: a same-user process or a planted file
reachability_vocabulary.operator: the user's or the agent's own command (A9)

fix_order.boundary: host → shared branch head, authored by a legitimate key
fix_order.chains: → AC-H-002 (same lie, per ref); feeds ST-E2-R1
fix_order.why: no key needed; the effect is a rewind other clones' guards see as a legitimate writer's push; the test reproduced the ref moving

fix_order.chains: entry of a chain: strip the policy, then serve forged history (needs A3) that the newcomer would otherwise refuse
fix_order.status: fixed this round; the withheld-index variant stays accepted under TM-R29
fix_order.why: no key needed to garble bytes; the clone silently ran without signatures-required

fix_order.boundary: host → the writer's belief about its own push
fix_order.chains: with AC-H-001: a host can make one clone think it pushed and another think the vault is empty
fix_order.why: integrity of the writer's view, not of the data; the user's next pull shows the truth, but an agent (A9) acting on 'pushed' does not pull

fix_order.chains: insider D4; with AC-C-001 (an emptied credential store resets silently) the loss is also silent
fix_order.why: reachable only by the user's own command or an agent's; the impact (every key and the credential store) is why it outranks its reachability ceiling of Medium: the scoring rubric caps on reachability, and the A9 actor makes 'operator' a real threat actor for this project

fix_order.reachability: local (the vault root the user chose)
fix_order.boundary: none crossed; the store splits in two under a path the type rewrote
fix_order.chains: with AC-L-006 (any ancestor .sg_vault is accepted): a sanitised path and an unexpected root compound
fix_order.status: reproduced (object_path); fix proposed, not applied this round (the type is used by every path field)
fix_order.why: a non-ASCII user name is common; the consequences (uninit leaves ciphertext and keys behind, backups miss the store) are integrity and confidentiality of local state

fix_order.boundary: host → compare-and-swap on the named ref
fix_order.chains: sibling of AC-H-001; partly closed by TM-F34 for clones with a baseline, open for the host's not_found on a ref the clone holds
fix_order.why: the host's word drops the CAS; fix is the same shape as TM-F34 (a held baseline makes not_found a rewind)

fix_order.reachability: read-key (an unrelated chain must still decrypt and, under the policy, be signed by a key that decrypts)
fix_order.chains: with ST-E2-S1 (TM-R01): a read-key holder's replacement chain longer than 50 commits is not a rewind to the guard
fix_order.why: UNKNOWN proceeds; the fix is to refuse UNKNOWN unless --accept-rewind

fix_order.boundary: host body text → client control flow
fix_order.chains: a flip to the static transport is a denial of writes for the process; no confidentiality path found (static passes no token)
fix_order.why: DoS-shaped; the rubric puts availability below integrity

fix_order.boundary: a planted ancestor .sg_vault → the user's next command
fix_order.chains: with TM-F22's per-vault server pin: the planted vault's server is authoritative, so the next push's token and data go there
fix_order.why: needs write access to an ancestor directory the user runs commands under (/tmp is the realistic one)

fix_order.boundary: a corrupt remotes.json → a different server
fix_order.why: the fall-through ends at the recorded default, which is the vault's own server in the common case; the TM-F22 pin may already catch it (open question to the verify dossier)

fix_order.chains: with TM-R26: lowering the floor lets old clients write again
fix_order.why: a writer can already do worse (TM-R13)

fix_order.reachability: local (a saved remote) / network once saved
fix_order.boundary: A2 on a remote the user marked no-verify once
fix_order.why: opt-in, equivalent to http:// (TM-R10), silent afterwards; a one-line warning fixes it
DoS (memory) from the host; a size cap is cheap

fix_order.boundary: a truncated vaults.enc → a silently reset credential store
fix_order.chains: with TM-F32 (now fixed) the two were the same loss
fix_order.why: loss of stored keys, not disclosure

fix_order.boundary: the stored token → a host the user typed
fix_order.why: a typo sends the token once; health-check without the token is cheap

fix_order.boundary: planted links or FIFOs in places only the user writes
fix_order.why: the same-user attacker can already edit the files; the fixes are the eed8084 pattern (lstat, O_NOFOLLOW, one reader) applied to the remaining readers

fix_order.reachability: host (each a narrower window than the ones above)
fix_order.boundary: host → client, with a check already in front of each
fix_order.why: each needs a specific state (a redirect hop, a retried CAS, a transient index read, a non-CAS data name, a backup member, a ref with a hostile commit_id, a withheld anchor) and the surrounding checks limit the effect

fix_order.reachability: varies (writer, local, operator, or the PKI messaging layer)
fix_order.why: robustness, consistency between readers, documentation claims, opt-in debug output, and a messaging-layer design note; none traced to a path that beats a control above it

undetermined.what_would_settle_it: whether the clone's private branch is ever read by another clone under signatures-required
whether Cache_Manager.rebuild_for_path verifies the fetched blob's content address
round 2: serve / mirror / publish own the static transport's callers

chains: AC-V-001 (strip the policy, host alone) → ST-E2-S1 / TM-R01 (serve forged history, read-key holder) → the newcomer accepts a forgery it would otherwise refuse. Entry closed this round (TM-F35); the withheld-index entry stays open under TM-R29
AC-H-001 (empty listing, host alone) → a stale clone plain-writes → ST-E2-R1 (the shared branch rewinds under a legitimate key). Closed this round (TM-F34)
AC-H-003 (empty reply) + AC-H-001: one clone believes it pushed, another believes the vault is empty; closed this round (TM-F33, TM-F34)
TM-F32 (pki delete ..) → AC-C-001 (an emptied store resets silently): the loss and the silence; the first closed, the second open
